speaker_role: student (Stanford undergrad) reviewing his own FERPA admissions file
commercial_incentive: channel 'Atlas Education' presents as a college-content creator/education brand; no explicit sales pitch in this transcript, but framing is promotional (subscribe/notifications asks)
key_insights: Stanford's internal committee prep form condenses an applicant to a short thematic summary plus codes telling the committee which parts of the file to read (e.g. roommate essay, extracurricular slate, family context)

Two independent readers each score six categories (high school rigor, support/recommendations, extracurriculars, self-presentation & intellectual vitality, test score, overall) roughly 1-5, where 1s and 2s overall are generally strong-to-automatic admits and 3s become a toss-up
Applicant's high school rigor was rated only a 3 despite his belief he'd taken a very competitive courseload, illustrating that rigor scoring is relative/unpredictable to the applicant
Reader 2 was notably more enthusiastic than Reader 1 and gave a 1 (best) in extracurriculars, which the applicant believes was the pivotal factor in his admit
Readers left explicit hedging language ('not sure who will emerge from pool, worth considering'), showing files can go to committee still undecided even when reviewers are positive
Interview scores were only average (3/3/3 across sub-categories) yet he was still admitted, suggesting the alumni interview carried limited weight relative to other file components

Reader notes repeatedly flagged one distinctive, deeply developed activity (a free tutoring nonprofit recognized by a U.S. senator) as elevating the file, supporting advice to go deep on one signature activity rather than spreading thin
specific_numbers_or_facts: Applicant self-reports an ACT superscore of 35/36, rated a 1 (best) in the testing category, per his file notes
Reader 1 gave: rigor 3, support 2, extracurriculars 2, self-presentation/intellectual vitality 3, overall 2, per the applicant's transcribed notes
Reader 2 gave: rigor 3, support 2, extracurriculars 1, self-presentation/intellectual vitality 2, overall '2 plus', per the applicant's transcribed notes
Applied Restrictive Early Action; committee voted to admit on November 27, 2021, per his file notes
notable_or_distinctive: A side note that readers mixed up his parents' occupations in their write-up shows admissions notes aren't always perfectly accurate, a useful reminder that file comments can contain errors.
reliability_notes: Same genre as prior Yale/Stanford FERPA file-review videos already in the knowledge base (different applicant, new data). Single self-reported account from handwritten notes taken during a time-limited, no-devices file viewing, so some terminology (e.g. 'SPIV', 'EC slate') may be misremembered or mistranscribed; channel may have a coaching/content business angle.
